purpose: Held-out English retrieval evaluation. Created after Steps 7–10 used the original 30 questions for architecture decisions. Do not edit to fit retrieval results.
how_to_use: The retrieval system must receive ONLY the 'question' field. Do not pass gold_sources, expected_answer_summary, or gold_evidence into the query.

questions.question: According to Bhagavad Gita 4.34, how should a person try to learn the truth?
questions.expected_answer_summary: By approaching a spiritual master, asking submissively, and serving him; self-realized souls can give knowledge because they have seen the truth.
questions.gold_evidence: slation  Just try to learn the truth by approaching a spiritual master. Inquire from him submissively and render service unto him. The self-realized souls can impart knowledge unto you because they have seen the truth.

questions.question: In Bhagavad Gita 6.35, what does Krishna say about controlling a restless mind?
questions.expected_answer_summary: It is difficult to curb the restless mind, but it is possible by suitable practice and detachment.
questions.gold_evidence: y-armed son of Kunté, it is undoubtedly very difficult to curb the restless mind, but it is possible by suitable practice and by detachment.

questions.question: What does Bhagavad Gita 7.7 say is superior to Krishna, and what image does He use for how everything rests on Him?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Nothing is superior to Krishna; everything rests on Him as pearls are strung on a thread.
questions.gold_evidence: lation  O conqueror of wealth, there is no truth superior to Me. Everything rests upon Me, as pearls are strung on a thread.

questions.question: According to Bhagavad Gita 9.22, what does Krishna say He does for those who worship Him with exclusive devotion?
questions.expected_answer_summary: He carries what they lack and preserves what they have.
questions.gold_evidence: ating on My transcendental form—to them I carry what they lack, and I preserve what they have.

questions.question: What does Bhagavad Gita 10.8 say about Krishna as the source of the worlds?
questions.expected_answer_summary: He is the source of all spiritual and material worlds; everything emanates from Him, and the wise who know this worship Him.
questions.gold_evidence: gavad-gita 10.8 — Translation  I am the source of all spiritual and material worlds. Everything emanates from Me. The wise who perfectly know this engage in My devotional service and worship Me with all their hearts.

questions.question: According to Bhagavad Gita 12.8, where should a person fix the mind and intelligence?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Fix the mind on Krishna and engage intelligence in Him; then one will live in Him.
questions.gold_evidence: Bhagavad-gita 12.8 — Translation  Just fix your mind upon Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and engage all your intelligence in Me. Thus you will live in Me always, without a doubt.

questions.question: What does Bhagavad Gita 17.15 describe as austerity of speech?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating others, and regularly reciting Vedic literature.
questions.gold_evidence: ech consists in speaking words that are truthful, pleasing, beneficial, and not agitating to others, and also in regularly reciting Vedic literature.

questions.question: In Bhagavad Gita 18.61, how does Krishna describe the Supreme Lord in relation to living beings wandering in the world?
questions.expected_answer_summary: The Supreme Lord sits in everyone’s heart and directs the wanderings of living beings, who are seated as on a machine made of material energy.
questions.gold_evidence: 8.61 — Translation  The Supreme Lord is situated in everyone’s heart, O Arjuna, and is directing the wanderings of all living entities, who are seated as on a machine, made of the material energy.

questions.question: At the end of the first chapter, what does Sanjaya say Arjuna did after speaking on the battlefield?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Arjuna threw down his bow and arrows and sat on the chariot, overwhelmed with grief.
questions.gold_evidence: having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.

questions.question: What chain of inner reactions does the Gita say begins when a person keeps thinking about sense objects?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Contemplating sense objects produces attachment, attachment produces lust, and lust produces anger.
questions.gold_evidence: Bhagavad-gita 2.62 — Translation  While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises.

questions.question: If someone leaves the body at the end of life while remembering Krishna alone, what does the Gita say happens?
questions.expected_answer_summary: That person at once attains Krishna’s nature; there is no doubt.
questions.gold_evidence: at the end of his life, quits his body, remembering Me alone, at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.

questions.question: Where does Krishna say He sits as the Supersoul, and how does He describe His relation to the beginning, middle, and end of all beings?
questions.expected_answer_summary: He is the Supersoul in the hearts of all living beings, and He is their beginning, middle, and end.
questions.gold_evidence: nslation  I am the Supersoul, O Arjuna, seated in the hearts of all living entities. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of all beings.

questions.question: After hearing Krishna describe Himself, what does Arjuna say he still wants to see about Krishna’s position in the universe?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Arjuna wants to see how Krishna has entered the cosmic manifestation—that form of His.
questions.gold_evidence: have described Yourself, I wish to see how You have entered into this cosmic manifestation. I want to see that form of Yours.

questions.question: When Krishna lists items in the process of knowledge, does He include approaching a genuine spiritual teacher along with qualities like humility and nonviolence?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Yes. The grouped verses list humility, pridelessness, nonviolence, and approaching a bona fide spiritual master among the process of knowledge.

questions.question: What does the Gita say happens to someone who serves Krishna in full devotion without fail, regarding the modes of nature?
questions.expected_answer_summary: That person immediately transcends the modes and comes to the level of Brahman.
questions.gold_evidence: unfailing in all circumstances, at once transcends the modes of material nature and thus comes to the level of Brahman.

questions.question: What three things does the Gita call gates leading to hell, which a sane person should give up?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Lust, anger, and greed are three gates to hell and should be given up.
questions.gold_evidence: re are three gates leading to this hell—lust, anger and greed. Every sane man should give these up, for they lead to the degradation of the soul.

questions.question: Should a knowledgeable person try to make less informed workers quit their ordinary jobs, or is there a better way to help them?
questions.expected_answer_summary: A learned person should not make ignorant workers stop; by working in devotion he should engage them in activities.
questions.gold_evidence: of prescribed duties, a learned person should not induce them to stop work. Rather, by working in the spirit of devotion, he should engage them in all sorts of activities [for the gradual development of Kåñëa consciousness].

questions.question: Is it safer, according to the Gita, to do someone else’s job perfectly than to do one’s own duty even if one does it imperfectly?
questions.expected_answer_summary: No. One’s own duty done imperfectly is better; following another’s path is dangerous.
questions.gold_evidence: Bhagavad-gita 3.35 — Translation  It is far better to discharge one’s prescribed duties, even though faultily, than another’s duties perfectly. Destruction in the course of performing one’s own duty is better than engaging in another’s duties, for to follow an

questions.question: What kind of seeing does the Gita praise when it talks about noticing stillness inside activity, and activity inside apparent stillness?
questions.expected_answer_summary: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is intelligent and transcendental even while active.
questions.gold_evidence: agavad-gita 4.18 — Translation  One who sees inaction in action, and action in inaction, is intelligent among men, and he is in the transcendental position, although engaged in all sorts of activities.

questions.question: How does true knowledge change the way a humble sage looks at a scholar, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and an outcaste?
questions.expected_answer_summary: By true knowledge they see those beings with equal vision.
questions.gold_evidence: ble sages, by virtue of true knowledge, see with equal vision a learned and gentle brähmaëa, a cow, an elephant, a dog and a dog-eater [outcaste].

questions.question: Why would a wise person refuse to chase pleasures that come from the senses, even if those pleasures feel good for a while?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Sense pleasures are sources of misery, they begin and end, so the wise do not delight in them.
questions.gold_evidence: ligent person does not take part in the sources of misery, which are due to contact with the material senses. O son of Kunté, such pleasures have a beginning and an end, and so the wise man does not delight in them.

questions.question: What makes someone a perfect yogi in how they relate to other people’s joy and pain, compared with their own?
questions.expected_answer_summary: A perfect yogi sees others’ happiness and distress as equal to his own.
questions.gold_evidence: by comparison to his own self, sees the true equality of all beings, in both their happiness and their distress, O Arjuna!

questions.question: The Gita mentions two ways of leaving this world, one bright and one dark. What is the difference in what happens afterward?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Passing in light, one does not come back; passing in darkness, one returns.
questions.gold_evidence: are two ways of passing from this world—one in light and one in darkness. When one passes in light, he does not come back; but when one passes in darkness, he returns.

questions.question: Can everyday acts like eating, giving, or performing austerity be turned into worship, according to the Gita?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Yes. Whatever one does, eats, offers, gives, or performs as austerity should be done as an offering to Krishna.
questions.gold_evidence: Bhagavad-gita 9.27 — Translation  Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give away, and whatever austerities you perform—do that, O son of Kunté, as an offering to Me.

questions.gold_evidence: spiritual advancement. In other words, indiscriminate charity is not recommended in the Vedic literature.

questions.question: How does this Gita distinguish sannyasa, the renounced order, from tyaga, renunciation?
questions.expected_answer_summary: Sannyasa is giving up activities based on material desire; tyaga is giving up the results of all activities.
questions.gold_evidence: sire is what great learned men call the renounced order of life [sannyäsa]. And giving up the results of all activities is what the wise call renunciation [tyäga].

questions.gold_evidence: beginning of creation, the three words oà tat sat were used to indicate the Supreme Absolute Truth. These three symbolic representations were used by brähmaëas while chanting the hymns of the Vedas and during sacrifices for the satisfaction of the Supreme.
